editorial:
Imagine a fancy house in Sydney where everyone is just waiting for the lady of the house to finally pass away. You get to meet Elizabeth Hunter, who is on her deathbed, and her two children who have rushed back from England. Sir Basil is a famous actor who is actually broke, and Dorothy is a princess who has seen better days. They aren't there out of love; they are there to make sure they get their hands on a huge pile of money. The vibe is very tense and a bit awkward, as you watch these greedy family members clash with the nurses and staff who actually take care of the dying woman.

What really makes this work is the acting, which feels very real and grounded. You will notice how the tension builds slowly, making the dialogue feel sharp and biting. While the story moves at a slower pace, it keeps you interested because you want to see who wins the money. If you enjoy character dramas with a bit of a mean streak, you should definitely give this one a try. For the best experience, try renting it on Apple TV or adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection to see the beautiful Australian scenery in high detail.
endingExplained: Everything comes to a head when Elizabeth finally passes away. Instead of a simple hand-off of wealth, the family deals with the fallout of their own greed and lies. You see the masks fall off as the siblings realize that their mother knew exactly how selfish they were. The movie ends by showing that the money cannot fix their broken lives, leaving you with a feeling of irony as they face their empty futures.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves family feuds and smart dialogue.
